LESSON: READING 5.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.2: Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should we read widely?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read a variety of familiar materials independently to build reading speed and fluency
2. apply appropriate strategies to read independently for information and enjoyment

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 5.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 5.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Read a variety of familiar materials independently to build reading speed and fluency

What this means
In this part you learn to read a variety of familiar materials independently to build reading speed and fluency. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read a variety of familiar materials independently to build reading speed and fluency.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read a variety of familiar materials independently to build reading speed and fluency. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Apply appropriate strategies to read independently for information and enjoyment

What this means
In this part you learn to apply appropriate strategies to read independently for information and enjoyment. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply appropriate strategies to read independently for information and enjoyment.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply appropriate strategies to read independently for information and enjoyment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read a variety of familiar materials independently to build reading speed and fluency)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading to a partner. (skill: apply appropriate strategies to read independently for information and enjoyment)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: read a variety of familiar materials independently to build reading speed and fluency.
3. Practise this skill: apply appropriate strategies to read independently for information and enjoyment.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we read widely?
2. What materials do you enjoy reading?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 5.2.1 Extensive Reading means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: read a variety of familiar materials independently to build reading speed and fluency.
5. Be able to: apply appropriate strategies to read independently for information and enjoyment.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
